name: Greater Albania
summary: Greater Albania (also called Ethnic Albania or Natural Albania) is a nationalist and irredentist idea that Albanians divided by the borders of 1913 should live in one state, taking in Kosovo and parts of North Macedonia, Montenegro, southern Serbia and Greek Chameria. Its carriers have ranged from the League of Prizren and wartime nationalists to the KLA and small groups such as the ANA. Today it is mostly held as a cultural and political aspiration of unification by consent, often alongside EU and NATO aims, and the idea itself carries no social or economic programme.
scope: The pan-Albanian national-unification claim as documented for the 1878 League of Prizren, the 1912 independence, the WWII unification, the KLA and post-1990 nationalists, and the contemporary mainstream that seeks unification by referendum or alongside EU integration. It excludes the Hoxha communist regime's non-irredentist policy and the violent fringe (ANA) except where noted. Economic and social answers are inferred and low confidence because the idea defines a territorial goal only.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Adherents range from free-market nationalists to left-wing ones such as Vetëvendosje, so the ideology is indifferent.

property-fundamental.rationale: Not part of the idea; adherents divided between liberal and left-wing parties.

worker-ownership.rationale: Nothing in the concept supports it; classed as outside a national-unification agenda and mostly opposed by its centre-right adherents.

state-harmful.rationale: The whole project aims at building a bigger, unified nation-state, which anarchism contradicts.

decide-locally.rationale: Ideology wants unification into one state, but also autonomy for Albanian areas; split.

abortion-legal.rationale: No ideological line; adherents split by religion (Muslim, Catholic, Orthodox) and by party.

more-religion-public.rationale: Albanianism put nation above religion, and the League of Prizren leadership wanted an identity cutting across faiths.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Cultural and linguistic unity of Albanians, with Illyrian continuity myths, is the basis of the claim to one nation.

gradual-change.rationale: Greater Albania seeks redrawing borders, but mainstream adherents now pursue it peacefully; leans against deferring to existing institutions.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Adherents look to the EU and NATO for Albanian integration but resent outside-imposed borders; split.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Kosovo Albanians welcomed the 1999 NATO intervention to stop Serbian repression.

open-borders.rationale: Borders dividing Albanians are the grievance, so open borders among Albanian lands are favoured, though not generally.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The idea has nothing to say on climate; adherents follow their parties' differing environmental stances.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy policy is unrelated to the claim; Albania's own energy debates are hydro-based and not tied to nationalism.

revolution-justified.rationale: Albanian national movements justified armed uprising against Ottoman, Yugoslav and Serbian rule (Kaçak, KLA), though mainstream now disavows violence for borders.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: A nation-state-building nationalism has no place for abolishing money; clearly outside the idea.

one-party-rule.rationale: Albania's one-party communist state under Hoxha was the period when nationalism and the Kosovo cause were sidelined; adherents today work through multiparty politics.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Zog's monarchy did not pursue irredentism; adherents split between republicans and monarchists.

democracy-best.rationale: Current adherents work through elections and referendums, but the concept is not a theory of government.

direct-votes.rationale: Adherents call for a referendum on unification, implying support for direct votes on this major question.

right-to-secede.rationale: Kosovo Albanians claim self-determination up to secession, citing the 1943 Bujan declaration.

natural-rulers.rationale: Albanian nationalism claims popular national self-rule; no doctrine of natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: The KLA and Kaçak tradition used violence and are venerated, while ICG notes violence for borders is unpopular; adherents split.

separate-church-state.rationale: Albanianism claims a secular national identity above Muslim, Catholic and Orthodox divisions.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Albanian nationalism is multi-faith and deliberately secular as its unifying principle.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Greater Albania defines the nation by Albanian ethnicity and language, claiming lands for their Albanian populations.

class-struggle-history.rationale: National struggle against partition is the organising frame, not class.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Albanian nationalists claim grievances against Ottoman, Serb and Greek rule, but not colonial reparations as such, so the idea stays neutral.

civilizational-union.rationale: Albanianism puts nation over religion, so union on shared faith is not its model.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bioethics lie outside a territorial national project.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Cryptography policy is unrelated to the unification claim.

restore-past-order.rationale: Restoration of the 1878 or 1943 maps is a motif, but the rebirth is toward a future national state; split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Adherents are driven by a nationalist goal but argue pragmatically about means; no clear stance either way.

direct-action.rationale: Kaçak and KLA direct action coexist with electoral politics today; split.

means-match-ends.rationale: Methods debates among adherents range from peaceful referendum to armed struggle, so there is no single position.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A distribution principle is not part of the idea; carriers differ on left and right.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Hoxha-style communism sidelined the Albanian national question; the idea is nationalist, not class-dictatorial.

taxation-theft.rationale: No libertarian element; the project assumes a taxing state.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Claims are for national, collective rights of Albanians across borders.

media-academia-power.rationale: The concept has no theory of media or university influence.

total-state.rationale: The nationalism is not totalitarian; communist total state is associated with its suppression.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Greater Albania seeks to enlarge the state, but through unification of co-ethnics rather than power projection.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Albanian nationalists contest Serb and Greek historiography, but no general epistemic doctrine is documented.

universal-morality.rationale: Moral philosophy is not a part of the idea; adherents hold varied religious and secular views.

single-common-good.rationale: The concept speaks of one national interest but there is no stated theory of a rationally derived common good.

revive-national-language.rationale: Albanian was never out of use, so the question rarely arises; though language is central to the national idea.

economic-freedom.rationale: Adherents run from liberal-market to left-developmental, so the idea is indifferent.

national-self-determination.rationale: The resolution promises the Albanian people of Kosovo the right to decide their own fate by self-determination, even to secession.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Albanianism is secular as a national identity, but adherents include many believers, so there is no consistent stance.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cultural heritage is the core of the national claim; inconsistent.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Albanians themselves suffered discrimination as minorities, and the movement does not advocate segregation.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy extraction policy has no bearing on the unification claim.

national-mission.rationale: Albanian nationalism is defensive and unificatory, not missionary.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not a doctrine; Albanian nationalism is multi-faith and national, not racial.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The question comes from Marxist debate and is not relevant to Albanian nationalism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Adherents argue for referendums and self-determination of Albanian populations.

trade-surplus.rationale: No trade doctrine is documented for the idea; adherents look chiefly to EU integration.

population-transfer.rationale: Serb expulsions in WWII were a documented outcome, but adherents officially claim minority protection and demand Cham return; split lean no.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Armed struggle is part of the tradition.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Albanian parties have both been banned and defended; no adherent line is documented on banning parties.

vanguard-party.rationale: Hoxha's party-state is the opposite of the pan-Albanian programme.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Poverty is widespread in the region but the concept does not give the poor priority; adherents are split.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing question that has no bearing on Albanian nationalism.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The concept stresses demography as strength, but takes no stand on population as a cause of poverty.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not an idea in Albanian nationalism and no adherent view is documented.

party-controls-media.rationale: Associated with the communist regime that suppressed the national cause.

party-commands-army.rationale: Associated with the communist regime, not the pan-Albanian programme.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Albanian governments and nationalists in Kosovo want EU membership, and see integration as a way to overcome divided borders.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Nationalists call for national solidarity in war.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: No documented adherent stance on censoring art; cultural expression is mainly valued as national heritage.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing tenure policy is outside the concept.

people-in-arms.rationale: KLA and guerrilla tradition support, modern national armies the norm; split.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Highland mythology exists, but not a doctrine.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The Bujan resolution says Kosovo and the Dukagjin plateau have always wanted to be united with Albania and sets out how that union is to be won.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Anti-intellectualism is not part of the idea, and nationalist movements include many intellectuals, so it is a split.

death-penalty.rationale: Albania and Kosovo abolished it, and nationalists have not made it an issue, so there is no consistent position.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Ethnic-nation framing and diaspora emphasis; documented in the ethnic basis of Greater Albania.

minority-language-support.rationale: Albanians in Yugoslavia suffered language discrimination, and the ICG records Ohrid Agreement language provisions as a gain.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Hoxha's isolation and repression are not seen as a model.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property theory is outside the concept and adherents differ by party.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Marxist classification debates have no bearing on Albanian nationalism.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Kosovo's incorporation into Yugoslavia at Prizren 1945 by a handpicked group is regarded as imposed, not consented.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Hoxha banned religion in 1967, but adherents today defend multi-faith pluralism; split.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Albanians opposed Serbian military suppression of Kosovo, so they reject force to hold a region.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale rests on general self-government, separate laws or no stated position, not on keeping a distinct economic system, and the statement now asks only whether a region joining a larger state should be free to keep its economic system.

reviewHistory.rationale: League of Prizren sought an autonomous province within the Ottoman Empire; Ohrid-style autonomy is accepted.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale rests on general self-government, separate laws or no stated position, not on keeping a distinct economic system, and the statement now asks only whether a region joining a larger state should be free to keep its economic system.

character-from-environment.rationale: Nature-nurture is not an issue for the concept, although the idea emphasises inherited ethnic identity, so it is a split.

leader-cult.rationale: Hoxha's cult is associated with the regime that suppressed national claims.

land-redistribution.rationale: Estate breakup was part of both interwar Albanian politics and communism, but the concept itself takes no side.

refugee-return.rationale: The Cham expulsion from Greece in 1945 and property claims are a central Albanian grievance; ICG says the Chams' grievances are legitimate.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The resolution grounds Kosovo's union with Albania in the region being inhabited by an Albanian majority.

women-must-cover.rationale: Secular Albanianism does not require this.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The defining aim is one state for Albanians, not minority autonomy inside existing states, though the League of Prizren first sought autonomy.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The KLA and ANA used armed force, but the mainstream now seeks unification by consent, so a mild yes is contested among adherents.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The 1912-13 borders set by the great powers split Albanian lands, and the project is built on undoing that division.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Greater Albania is a claim on Albanian-inhabited lands left outside the 1913 borders, though adherents mostly seek unification by consent rather than a war-loss claim.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The idea has no land policy; adherents are split between protectionist nationalism and openness to investment.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: No stance in the core territorial idea and no evidence of adherents split either way.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The KLA drew external backing and diaspora funds, and the ICG report describes support for Albanian armed groups abroad.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: No position stated; nationalists favour sovereignty but depend on EU and diaspora funds.

job-guarantee.rationale: No economic programme is attached to the idea, so adherents are split.

industrial-unions.rationale: The idea has no labour programme; adherents are split.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The mainstream does not frame Serbs or other minorities as a hidden conspiracy, though grievance narratives exist.

informal-organisation.rationale: The League of Prizren was a formal national organisation, and unification is pursued through parties and institutions.

religious-nation.rationale: Albanian nationalism defines the nation by language and ethnicity across Muslim, Catholic and Orthodox Albanians, not by a shared religion.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: No health or services policy in the idea; carriers differ, so neutral.

socialized-care.rationale: No documented position on family care; carriers differ, so neutral.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The project is grounded in Albanians' historical presence in Kosovo and neighbouring lands, including Illyrian-descent claims, as the Wikipedia and ICG accounts describe.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The idea carries no model of democracy; adherents are split by party.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not part of a territorial nationalism; adherents are split.

alienated-labor.rationale: No economic programme in the core idea.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Albanian nationalism treats Albanians as a European nation and the mostly Muslim population as part of Europe, and carriers seek EU and NATO membership.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The idea rests on national self-determination, as in the 1912 declaration, not divine authority.

social-market-economy.rationale: No economic programme in the core idea; adherents span left and right.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The KLA and the nationalist tradition rest on armed struggle for unification, and Albanians seek NATO membership and armed forces.

rich-first.rationale: No economic programme in the core idea.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Albanian nationalists historically had republican, king (Zog) and communist phases; the movement is about territory, not dynastic rule, and modern carriers favour republics.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not part of the project; adherents hold varied economic views.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: A territorial nationalism with no documented position; its carriers are split between EU-integrationist and sovereigntist stances.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Albanian nationalism is notable for religious tolerance across Muslim, Orthodox and Catholic Albanians, a point stressed in national narrative; marriage restrictions by religion contradict that unity.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The movement's unity claim rests on Albanians across Muslim and Christian faiths, so religious boycotts of fellow nationals would contradict it.

rent-control.rationale: The idea carries no housing programme, so adherents are not divided on a position that is simply not part of it.

abolish-ip.rationale: The idea carries no economic programme, so this is not a position adherents hold either way.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The KLA and earlier armed struggles for unification and independence show adherents accept lethal force in defence of the nation.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Illyrian continuity theory is described as the founding myth of Albanian nationhood and is used to support claims to Kosovo and other lands.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The central aim is to gather divided Albanians into one state, not to leave them in a cultural diaspora around a homeland.

culture-before-state.rationale: The League of Prizren stressed language and culture before statehood, but the 1912 independence and the later aim of one state were political, so adherents are split.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Bujan treats the Albanian-majority lands of Kosovo and Dukagjin as belonging in one state with Albania rather than in Yugoslavia.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The project organises Albanians as one national-ethnic community across state borders, so adherents back organising to defend that group's interests; the sources frame it as ethnic nationhood rather than race as such.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in Albanian ancestry and national culture runs through the movement's history from the League of Prizren on, though the sources speak of nation rather than race.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The ICG and Wikipedia accounts define the idea as uniting Albanians divided by the 1913 borders into one state on the basis of shared language and national identity.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Albanian nationalists see the 1913 borders as imposed by the Great Powers and neighbouring states, which supports a lean to agree, though sources vary.

free-public-college.rationale: The idea is a territorial goal with no education policy; adherents' parties differ on tuition.

pollution-taxes.rationale: The idea carries no environmental programme, and adherents are not united on how to protect it.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on women's distinct roles, giving their values more weight, a claim about innate nature or no stated position, and the statement now asks only whether women tend to be more compassionate than men.

reviewHistory.rationale: The idea carries no gender programme; adherents are not clearly for or against giving women's values extra weight.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on women's distinct roles, giving their values more weight, a claim about innate nature or no stated position, and the statement now asks only whether women tend to be more compassionate than men.

capital-controls.rationale: The idea carries no economic programme and adherents are split between market and state-led views.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The idea concerns territory, not arms control; mainstream carriers seek a normal state with a single army, though the KLA's armed origins make this a mild inference.

collective-bargaining.rationale: No labour doctrine; the idea is a territorial goal and adherents span left and right on economics.

sacred-nation.rationale: Pan-Albanian nationalism treats the Albanian nation as a community of shared history, language and fate worth unifying across borders, as the League of Prizren and 1912 declaration show; 'sacred' is a stronger word than sources use.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Albanian nationalists describe Serbian rule over Kosovo as foreign domination, but the statement is about a wealthy centre exploiting its own poorer regions, which the idea does not address.

premarital-sex.rationale: The idea carries no social programme, and the Albanian mainstream is split on it.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Albanian nationalists in North Macedonia, southern Serbia and Montenegro have sought territorial autonomy where Albanians are the majority, as the ICG report describes.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Contemporary adherents seek unification by referendum, and the nationalist case rests on the self-determination of Albanian-majority areas.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about defending or claiming the homeland, not a spiritual bond with it, which is all the statement now asks about.

reviewHistory.rationale: The idea rests on a national homeland of Albanians that should be united, as in the 1878 League of Prizren and the 1912 independence claims.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about defending or claiming the homeland, not a spiritual bond with it, which is all the statement now asks about.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Protecting Albanians left outside Albania's borders by the 1913 settlement is the core of the project.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The idea carries no economic programme, and adherents are split.

self-ownership.rationale: The idea carries no social or economic programme, and adherents are split.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The idea carries no economic programme, and adherents are split.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The idea carries no social programme, and adherents are split.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: No economic position follows from the idea; adherents are split.

missingStatements.text: The Albanian language and culture should be the basis for one nation-state of all Albanians.
missingStatements.rationale: The ICG and Wikipedia accounts define the project as joining Albanian-inhabited lands into one national state on cultural and linguistic grounds.

missingStatements.text: Citizens of a region should be able to vote in a referendum on joining a neighbouring state where their nationality is the majority.
missingStatements.rationale: Contemporary adherents (for example Vetëvendosje) call for unification by referendum, per the Wikipedia accounts.

missingStatements.text: Leaders should be able to claim territory based on ancient descent from the region's first inhabitants.
missingStatements.rationale: The Illyrian continuity theory is described as the founding myth of Albanian nationhood and used to support claims to Kosovo.
missingStatements.declined: A justification for claims already covered by reunify-divided-nation and co-ethnic-territorial-claim, not a separate position.

notes: Positions vary by strand: the League of Prizren sought only autonomy within the Ottoman Empire, Hoxha and Zog did not pursue irredentism, the KLA and ANA used force, and most current adherents want unification by consent or a Kosovo-Albania partnership. Polls cited on Wikipedia show widely varying support for unification.
